verdict.line: You lose if you trade into Parrrley and passive poison stacks before level 6 with no wave control; you win if you pull the lane, bank Q stacks, and start Withering him into forced all-ins once Fury of the Sands is up.

brief.thesis: Gangplank fights you at 625 range with Q (Parrrley, 5s cooldown) and stacks magic poison off every auto from his passive (Grog-Soaked Blade), while your Q (Siphoning Strike) only reaches 255 — you cannot out-poke him, you can only out-scale him. Every game is decided by whether you minimize free damage early so your stack count and items carry you past him later.

theirWindow.when: Parrrley is up and you're near minions
theirWindow.what: He'll land free Q pokes plus passive poison on anything he can last-hit near you. Back off the creep line and let the wave come to you so he has to walk into melee to punish you.

yourWindow.when: Wither is up, he's engaged or low HP
yourWindow.what: Land W (Wither, 700 range) the moment he commits to a trade or extends past minions — it cuts his Attack Speed and Movement Speed, and Remove Scurvy only clears CC and heals him, it does nothing to stop the slow itself.

start.why: The flat HP and regen directly answer his passive poison ticks and Parrrley chip damage while you're stuck farming at 255 range.

boots.why: The ability haste tightens your Q/W/E loop so Wither comes back faster and Spirit Fire is live for more trades.

core.why: Gives you the stats and proc damage to actually win extended trades once you've caught up on stacks.
The Attack Speed slow on nearby enemies blunts his on-hit poison application rate.
Amplifies your Soul Eater lifesteal and ability-based healing for sustained side-lane duels.

situational.when: he's leaning on sustained autos and passive poison damage to win fights
their team has stacked crit or AD carries beyond just Gangplank
you need more wave clear and AoE slow instead of raw dueling power

runes.keystoneWhy: The healing and Movement Speed on hit let you take free farm hits from his poke and still reposition out of his effective range before he can follow up.

summoners.why: Teleport lets you reset off a pulled, stack-farmed lane without losing tempo, and Ghost closes the gap on a Gangplank who has no hard CC to punish the engage — only slows from Cannon Barrage.

playing.title: Pull the wave to your tower
playing.detail: Standing back forces him to walk into melee range to contest minions, cutting off free Parrrley pokes and passive poison stacks.

playing.title: Bank every Q stack you can
playing.detail: Siphoning Strike's damage only grows on kills — prioritize last-hitting with Q over trading damage you can't win early.

playing.title: Drop Spirit Fire before you commit
playing.detail: Spirit Fire (12s cooldown, 650 range) shreds his armor before you walk in, making your follow-up autos and Q hit harder.

playing.title: Wither on cooldown once it's up
playing.detail: Wither's slow on Movement and Attack Speed is not removed by Remove Scurvy, so use it the instant he extends to fight or disengage.

playing.title: Avoid even trades before level 6
playing.detail: Without Fury of the Sands you lose straight damage races to his ranged Q plus on-hit poison — just farm.

playing.title: All-in off Fury of the Sands
playing.detail: Once Fury of the Sands (120s cooldown, 400 range) is up, its max Health gain and HP drain let you force fights he can't just heal away from.

playing.title: Punish poison stacking with Thornmail
playing.detail: If his passive damage is carrying his trades, Thornmail turns his free autos into a liability.

brief.patchCaveat: All win rates, sample sizes, and the full build/rune/summoner data above are measured from real games on the current patch (16.20.1) via OP.GG; the matchup read — why the numbers shake out this way — is my own tactical analysis, not sourced data.

stats.opponentTip: Keep your distance from Gangplank to avoid being hit by his Grasp of the Undying + (Q) and (P) basic attacks. Pull lane and farm with [Q] to gain stacks, while looking for an opportunity post-level 6
